## 固定收益市場主軸

9月21日，油價回落，加上外交斡旋重現希望，緩解了全球市場壓力，帶動較長天期美國公債上漲；聯準會官員則強調通膨仍須以緊縮政策應對，使短端殖利率居高不下。10年期殖利率下降5個基點至4.96%，回到5%以下，2年期則持平於4.76%。股市也同步回升，Meta人工智慧代理程式引發的熱潮帶動科技股走高，美國高收益債利差則變動不大。

這波債市漲勢主要來自實質殖利率下降，並非長期通膨補償回落。油價下跌雖讓市場喘息，貨幣政策的分歧卻未因此消失：芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee警告，供給衝擊反覆出現，可能迫使聯準會採取令經濟承受痛苦的緊縮措施；聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem則認為，現行政策仍屬寬鬆。借款人仍持續籌資。軟銀啟動逾$110億融資，支應對OpenAI的投資；卡達雖因戰爭蒙受出口收入損失，仍以大幅低於初步指引的利差募得$30億。

## 美國公債回升，短端未隨之走強

美國公債的漲勢隨天期拉長而更為明顯。5年期殖利率下降3個基點至4.83%，30年期下降5個基點至5.29%；2年期未動，帶動2年與10年期利差收窄5個基點至20個基點。不過，本月以來2年期殖利率仍上升52個基點，高於10年期的22個基點。週一買盤壓低了較長期融資成本，但市場先前對近期聯準會政策路徑的重新定價，幾乎未被扭轉。

10年期抗通膨公債（TIPS）實質殖利率下降6個基點至2.62%，同天期損益兩平通膨率反而上升1個基點至2.34%。紐約下午5時固定收益市場收盤時，布蘭特原油期貨報每桶$96.12，下跌7.46%；西德州原油期貨報$92.06，下跌8.22%。能源價格下跌雖減輕了消費者與企業眼前的負擔，長期通膨補償卻未同步降低；名目殖利率下滑仍由實質利率下降帶動。

川普總統表示，可能願意在聯合國大會期間與伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian會面，讓外交解決的希望升溫。衛星觀測也顯示，週末沙烏地阿拉伯在波斯灣內的石油裝船量增加，其主要海灣港口的船舶數量為6月以來最多。

然而，荷莫茲海峽航運仍嚴重受阻。路透統計，週末有17艘商品運輸船通過，少於一週前的37艘；2月28日戰爭爆發前，通常每天約有125艘大型商船行經海峽。部分油輪關閉船舶識別訊號航行，因此可觀測到的船舶活動無法涵蓋全部出口。9月13日當週，共有22艘油輪駛出海峽，大多為超大型原油輪，載運4,200萬桶原油；其中沙烏地阿拉伯與伊拉克各占43%。沙國紅海港口延布則自9月16日以來未見石油裝船活動。

美中磋商另為市場情緒帶來支撐。美國財政部長Scott Bessent表示，週末與中國國務院副總理何立峰等官員會談，已同意展開AI對話，就目標與威脅建立共同認知。美國貿易代表Jamieson Greer則表示，貿易理事會已開始運作，可能涵蓋有限範圍的非敏感商品，包括中國消費品與低科技產品，以及美國能源、農業與醫療產品。不過，《金融時報》報導，這輪磋商並未延長貿易休戰，實質決定仍留待領袖會晤。

當天公布的8月芝加哥聯準銀行全國經濟活動指數，從修正後的0.08降至-0.04，低於預期的0.2，顯示整體成長轉弱。但兩位聯準會官員仍著重說明，通膨持續偏高何以可能需要進一步緊縮。

Goolsbee週一在倫敦指出，供給干擾出現得更頻繁、持續更久，造成的損害也更大，不能再將反覆衝擊一概視為暫時性的物價水準變動。為恢復物價穩定，聯準會可能必須抑制需求，範圍甚至超出成本最初上升的產業，就業、薪資與成長都可能因此受損。

他也保留了重要區別：面對供給衝擊，緊縮力道未必須與抑制需求過熱時同樣強烈；但若對反覆且持續的衝擊不作回應，就無法履行維持物價穩定的職責。這與政府主張聯準會不應在能源衝擊期間升息的立場相左。主席Kevin Warsh的看法也有所不同，他在政策會議後曾表示，通膨降至2%未必需要以勞動市場受損為代價。

今年在聯邦公開市場委員會沒有投票權的Musalem，在路透專訪中更直接主張加強緊縮。他認為目前3.75%至4.00%的政策目標區間仍屬寬鬆；若不進一步收緊，18個月後通膨仍明顯高於2%的可能性，大於回到目標的可能性。據他判斷，排除石油及其他供給因素影響後的基礎通膨，可能仍比目標高約1個百分點，而且方向持續惡化。7月個人消費支出（PCE）物價年增率為3.7%，高於2025年4月近期低點的2.3%。

Musalem傾向及早、小幅逐步升息，認為這比等到通膨更根深蒂固後再大幅行動，對經濟的干擾較小，但未指明下一步或終點利率。兩人的論述說明了油價好轉何以未能消除短端壓力：他們都把通膨持續性視為不同於最新油價變動的問題。

股市受惠的範圍較廣。標普500指數上漲1.49%至7,764.70，那斯達克100上漲2.83%，半導體指數上漲4.29%。Meta的Muse代理程式受到歡迎，重燃市場對運算需求的期待，帶動Meta上漲11%；AMD上漲10%，收盤市值首次突破$1兆。美元指數上升0.20%至100.425，黃金期貨下跌0.51%至每盎司$4,402.20。當日債券與科技股同步上漲，風險偏好回升，卻未伴隨資金全面撤離美元。

## AI舉債規模擴大，投資人重新審視融資條件

軟銀的融資計畫由先前洽談推進至正式啟動發債，擬發行$100億美元計價優先無擔保債，以及€10億歐元債。美元券分為3.5年、5.5年與7.5年期，歐元券則為4年與6年期。交易總額折合約$111.5億，若完成將超越7-Eleven於2021年1月發行的$109.3億，成為亞太及日本非金融企業歷來最大筆公司債發行。

募集資金將用於軟銀追加投資OpenAI的第三期$100億款項，以及一般企業用途；該期投資預計10月1日完成交割。新債將取代先前已取得的$100億過橋融資，預計9月24日定價、9月29日交割，惠譽給予擬發行債券BB+評等。軟銀先前已擴大有擔保借款能力，如今再向公開債市投資人提出大額無擔保融資需求。

這筆交易也將推高軟銀今年已相當龐大的發債量。據彭博報導，軟銀此前已發行各幣別債券合計近$150億，是2026年最大垃圾債評級發行人。其2031年到期美元債的殖利率，本月稍早升至8.2%，遠高於1月低點6.7%，反映信用利差及作為基準的美國公債殖利率同步上升。儘管股市對AI的熱情回溫，AI投資的融資成本已提高，新債將檢驗投資人是否願意再增加曝險。

週一稍晚，維吉尼亞州里奇蒙附近的Digital Drive資料中心專案也開始推介約$11億垃圾債融資。這項消息在美國固定收益市場收盤後傳出，由高盛牽頭的銀行團正為建設籌資，專案由Blue Owl Capital、Cedarwood Investment Group及PowerHouse Data Centers的關係企業支持，初步殖利率洽談落在9%區間的低端至中段。

Digital Drive全部76百萬瓦IT容量將租予CoreWeave，合約期限15年、總額$29.4億，預計2027年至2028年間開始營運。長約提供了長期收入承諾，但設施尚未營運就需要資金；對租戶未具投資等級評等的專案，投資人一直要求較高殖利率。投資人電話會議訂於週二紐約時間上午10時，預計週三定價。

富達國際的James Durance對AI債務擴張抱持疑慮。這位管理$140億資產的經理人，將旗下收益策略的科技業曝險維持在2%以下，並認為到明年底，放款規模本身就會成為風險來源。他的全球收益與短存續期間策略不受基準指數約束，因此即使科技業在指數中的權重提高，也不必跟進配置。

Durance擔心的不只是個別違約。企業已對今年及明年作出龐大支出承諾，卻很少提供更遠期的指引；若這些投資無法帶來足夠報酬，成長預期與風險資產可能同受打擊。他並未把AI引發衰退列為基本情境，但指出，超大型雲端業者債務的存續期間偏長，所帶來的利率敏感度與其債務規模不成比例。彭博科技債指標過去一年約下跌2.4%，跌幅大於全球綜合債券指數的1.3%。

他轉而配置英國銀行與企業的投資等級債及高收益債，並選擇部分新興市場借款人的強勢貨幣計價債券，包括土耳其Akbank與Turkcell，以及墨西哥、羅馬尼亞和菲律賓主權債。即使新AI融資案仍持續進入市場，這些配置也呈現了投資人因應AI融資規模與估值的一種做法。

歐洲央行管理委員會委員Fabio Panetta週一演說則提出另一層考量。他表示，對AI獲利的樂觀期待有助科技企業籌資並持續投資，但若盈餘不如預期，估值也容易受衝擊。義大利央行估算，廣泛採用AI可使義大利每年勞動生產力成長率提高逾1個百分點；Panetta強調，需求與通膨會如何變化，取決於收益由誰取得。

若新工作任務出現、預期勞動所得增加，提振家庭信心，消費便可能強化投資熱潮，使通膨延續更久；相反地，若自動化加深工作與薪資的不安全感，儲蓄增加、支出轉弱，通膨降溫可能更早出現。他將生產力收益的分配與規模同列為重要因素，而非假定所有AI投資增加都會帶來相同的貨幣政策結果。

新研究也量化了資料中心實際落成的障礙。Data Center Watch指出，4月至6月間，地方反對使美國45個專案遭阻擋或延後，總值$680億。有些社區甚至在開發商申請許可前就暫停核准建設，約30州的州議會也提出或通過涉及選址、電力與用水的規範。這些數據雖屬前一季，卻具體呈現了專案延誤的規模，以及以未來營運為基礎的融資計畫所面臨的風險。

相關資本需求並不止於資料中心，電力基礎設施也吸引大量投資。彭博新能源財經統計，2026年上半年中國以外地區的再生能源投資達$2,470億，年增15%；同期新增發電容量中，太陽能與電池儲能占70%。歐洲監管機關估計，當地老舊電網至2030年需要€6,000億投資。這些投資既為運算需求所帶動的資本支出增添規模，也是在因應能源供應風險。彭博報導，伊朗戰爭已加速菲律賓、泰國等逾10國的再生能源與儲能專案。

## 科技業以外，再融資機會也重現

暑期票房強勁，讓AMC Entertainment重新推進接近$40億的資本結構調整。這家電影院營運商啟動$20億垃圾債與$8.5億槓桿貸款銷售，並與德意志銀行簽署$11.2億第二順位擔保貸款承諾書；債券初步討論的殖利率位於9%區間低端。AMC希望藉營運復甦，置換2029年及2031年到期的定期貸款，以及AMC與子公司Muvico於2029年到期的債券。

營運改善幅度相當明顯。AMC表示，7月與8月合併營收年增42%至$13.3億，觀影人次增加36%。Rentrak統計，美國與加拿大電影院暑期票房達創紀錄的$47.7億。

六個月前，AMC才因市場條件不利，放棄債券與貸款再融資，改與德意志銀行困境資產產品部門承作$4.25億交易；該交易設有條款，若日後能進行更廣泛的再融資，可按較有利條件還款。6月30日AMC企業借款為$37億。週一啟動的新交易，是以改善後的營運表現再次爭取再融資，最終成本仍待確定。

Nuveen開始就首次英鎊債及三筆美元債與投資人舉行電話會議，部分資金將用於收購施羅德。英鎊券規劃為5年期。身為TIAA旗下投資管理公司的Nuveen，今年稍早同意以£99億收購施羅德，合併後主動式管理資產將接近$2.5兆。Nuveen已與法國巴黎銀行簽署最高£31億的收購融資額度，新債將支應部分現金需求及一般企業用途。法國巴黎銀行擔任全球協調人，美銀證券與摩根大通則為聯席簿記管理人。

歐洲電信業方面，高盛交易員在槓桿融資會議與管理層會面後，認為較短天期的債券可望受惠於個別企業改善，具體看好Virgin Media O2的2029年期債券及VodafoneZiggo的2030年期債券。兩家公司面對新興光纖網路日益激烈的競爭，流通在外債券分別超過$150億及接近$80億；投資人7月曾因擔憂獲利與償債能力而大幅拋售其債券。

交易員認為，Virgin Media O2的支持因素在於AI可能節省的成本，以及計畫收購Netomnia。VodafoneZiggo則可透過資產處分創造現金，包括已同意以€6.69億出售行動通訊基地台；調整定價與合約後，訂戶趨勢也在改善。該公司與Telenet合併後，管理層以2027年中前讓整個集團上市為目標。這些進展都有望改善償債能力。

墨西哥Fibra Educa正尋求批准，年底前以增額發行6月債券的方式，在本地再籌措MXN30億至MXN35億。執行長Raul Martinez Solares表示，資金將用於收購校園及可能的開發，可直接支付，也可償還先前用於收購的MXN25億循環信用額度。投資人將於週二開會，討論是否允許動用2023年設立的MXN200億債務計畫全額；該信託目前已達前五年適用的MXN120億上限，此外還須取得監管批准。管理層也在研究海外借款，但收入以披索計價，匯率曝險或避險成本構成實質限制。

證券化市場的發行條件相對有利。Truist的Brock Wolf預估，美國資產擔保證券（ABS）今年發行量最多可增長15%，2027年再增10%。目前發行量已連續第三年超過$3,000億，比2025年同期進度快11%，利差則處於逾四年最窄水準。Wolf預期資料中心支出與銀行合成風險移轉將是重要供給來源，主要不確定因素則是油價及聯準會對通膨的回應。

另一份法院文件揭露，陷入困境的商品交易商Radiant World存在集中的應收帳款融資風險。公司披露積欠六家債權人共$8.7億，以Jefferies與Intesa Sanpaolo曝險最大，其次為德意志銀行、瑞穗、Mariner Investment Group及Incomlend。文件確認了債權人與風險金額，但未確定可回收多少款項。

歐洲結算基礎設施週一也有新進展。歐洲央行啟用Pontes，將區塊鏈市場連接至既有歐元區支付系統，讓銀行可用央行貨幣結算代幣化大額交易。首批參與者與分散式帳本營運商已準備立即使用，其他機構計畫在未來幾個月接入。較長期的後續系統Appia預計2028年提出藍圖。Pontes讓這類交易得以使用央行貨幣結算，與規劃中的零售數位歐元是不同安排。

## 加拿大、南韓與南非的升息風險各有來源

加拿大央行總裁Tiff Macklem週一在哈利法克斯進一步警告：面對持續通膨，若太晚展開必要緊縮，日後可能被迫加快升息，最終利率也可能更高。但他也指出，若物價壓力仍受控就貿然升息，只會削弱成長，卻無相應效益。

加拿大央行正在評估，2.25%的政策利率能否使通膨回到2%。Macklem表示，消費者物價年增率一直在3%左右，主要受汽油影響；若油價維持每桶$100附近，未來幾個月通膨可能略升。他關注的是衝擊會持續多久，而不只是整體物價最初受到多大影響。

Macklem也提出美國貿易限制對成長的新估計：若最新關稅持續，第四季成長率可能約減半至1%以下。直接受影響商品只占加拿大對美商品出口約5%，聯邦支援亦可減輕部分損害；更廣泛的風險則是不確定性使企業延後招聘與投資。央行將在10月《貨幣政策報告》首次使用新預測模型Prima，以檢視不同情境，區分暫時與持續性的物價壓力。

南韓方面，摩根大通經濟學家Seok Gil Park認為，只要信用與金融市場維持穩定，即使該行已高於市場共識的3.75%終點利率預測，仍有上行風險。摩根大通預期，利率將從目前3%起，在11月、2月及5月陸續調升；相較之下，彭博經濟學家調查中位數為3.5%，並維持至2028年第二季。

摩根大通較鷹派的預測，來自對成長的判斷。Park預估今年成長3.8%、明年3.3%，高於南韓央行的3.3%與2.9%；第三季季增率方面，摩根大通估約1%，南韓央行則估約0.3%。半導體景氣熱潮已反映在投資，能否進一步擴散至供應商、薪資與家庭支出，將決定後續帶來多少額外國內通膨。

Park正在觀察非石油製造品與個人服務價格偏高的月增幅。韓元升值會降低進口成本，但他指出，若升值來自貿易條件改善及實質所得增加，也可能支撐需求。大型晶片製造商的高額獎金，直接受惠者只占勞工較小比例，單靠獎金對消費的推升可能有限。政策關鍵在於所得增加能否普及，而不只看半導體出口。

南非近期調查顯示通膨預期改善，但分析師的利率預測反而轉向更多緊縮。摩根士丹利Andrea Masia與Arnav Gupta將9月23日決策預測，由不變改為升息25個基點至7.25%。他們將此視為預防性措施，防止油價壓力再起、延長通膨高於3%目標的時間，並非因為通膨預期已惡化，或油價漲勢已廣泛傳導至消費者物價。

通膨升高，也會削弱名目利率不變時的實質緊縮程度。摩根士丹利預期南非央行此次升息後，將維持利率不變至2027年底，認為短期利率再反映市場目前定價約75個基點額外緊縮的空間有限。

美國銀行Tatonga Rusike則從原估一次升息，改為預期9月與11月各升息一次，使附買回利率達7.5%。他將通膨預測上修至第四季平均5%，2027年第一季達5.3%高峰，並預期降息將延後至2027年下半年。調查中的通膨預期則從3.9%微降至3.8%，凸顯分析師較鷹派的利率預測，著眼於未來油價的影響。

巴西央行每週調查則往相反方向調整。在上週降息至13.75%後，分析師將2026年底Selic利率預測由13.75%下修至13.5%，2027年與2028年預測則分別維持12%及10.50%。能否繼續寬鬆，部分取決於Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva與Flavio Bolsonaro勢均力敵的總統選戰將帶來何種財政與匯率影響。即使國內經濟降溫，公共債務與支出計畫仍可能牽動巴西雷亞爾及通膨。

人民幣並未跟隨美元走強而貶值。在岸匯價一度升至每美元6.6950元，收在6.6955，為2022年6月以來最強在岸收盤價。中國人民銀行將中間價設於6.7487，雖仍比路透估計弱536點，但9月以來調升速度加快，與市場預期的差距也縮小，顯示人行對人民幣在2%交易波幅內逐步升值的容忍度提高。

## 主權借款人的融資條件明顯分化

卡達完成11月以來首次公開國際發債，以5年與10年期債券募得$30億，定價利差分別為美國公債之上55與65個基點，均比初步定價想法收窄約30個基點。訂單高峰超過$77億，之後回落至約$68億；5年期高峰需求超過$30億，不含聯席主辦行認購意向，10年期則達$47億。

市場反應熱絡，與卡達出口收入重挫形成對比。荷莫茲海峽受阻，損及卡達主要出口通道，液化天然氣收入從第一季$90億降至第二季$2億。摩根大通指出，政府當季赤字達$58億，相當於季度GDP的11.4%，財政收入年減57%。彭博調查的經濟學家預估，卡達今年經濟將萎縮12.1%。

卡達仍有相當雄厚的財務緩衝，包括$5,800億主權財富基金與逾$700億外匯存底，並獲標普AA評等，投資計畫也持續推進。政府宣布成立Doha Investment，管理並擴大主權財富基金的國內投資組合，另規劃五年內授出約$385億基礎建設合約，包括公私協力案。卡達投資局則以與摩根大通建立$200億合作關係為目標，其中$150億用於公開市場股票，$50億用於美國中型企業的私募投資。但這些計畫並未消除眼前的財政衝擊。

智利本幣主權債持續吸引外資。8月非居民持有的披索債增加$7億，達創紀錄的$210.4億，較年初成長42%；增幅明顯高於哥倫比亞截至8月的4.2%，以及巴西、墨西哥截至7月約2%與3%的增幅。

財政表現有助解釋智利債券的吸引力。7月財政盈餘為CLP950億，一年前則是CLP9,570億赤字；民營礦業收入增加79%，支出減少0.7%。財政部長Jorge Quiroz計畫將明年支出增幅限制在0%至1%。Banco Itau的Andres Perez表示，在多年赤字超標之後，高金屬價格與支出節制正增強財政整頓的可信度。

市場准入改革也可能支撐外資需求。政府正爭取首次允許退休基金承作附買回及反向附買回交易，並就造市商計畫公開徵詢意見。退休基金提案屬於30項資本市場措施的一部分，其他措施也處理外資面對的文書與稅務障礙。Banco de Credito e Inversiones的Alexis Vega預期，附買回融資可降低投資成本，造市制度則可改善政府債券流動性。

波蘭週五遭穆迪降評後，首個交易日反應相對平靜。2036年到期美元債殖利率週一下降4個基點至5.86%；華沙早盤，本幣10年期債相對德國公債利差，從前一週高峰289個基點收窄至273個基點。茲羅提兌歐元升值0.1%。雖然政治分歧仍妨礙財政整頓，降至A3的評等並未立即引發新一波賣壓。

歐洲財政委員會則對財政規則的執行提出更廣泛警告：反覆給予彈性、啟用豁免條款，可能削弱2024年4月推出的新規則。新制給予各國四至七年，逐步朝歐盟赤字占GDP 3%、債務占GDP 60%的上限靠攏。委員會表示，迄今未發出任何「遵守或解釋」聲明，只有保加利亞面臨新啟動的過度赤字程序。歐盟債務占GDP比率從2024年的81%升至2025年的82%，歐盟執委會預估今年將超過84%。

俄羅斯也提高了融資需求。財政部長Anton Siluanov表示，2026年赤字將達GDP的3%，高於原定1.6%，也高於2025年的2.6%；1月至8月累積赤字已達2.5%。舉債將超過原先RUB5.5兆計畫，另以往年未動用資金補充。較高油價與較弱盧布雖增加出口相關收入，仍未阻止財政惡化，高利率也推升償債成本。Siluanov仍預期，國家財富基金準備將增加RUB6,000億至RUB1兆，年底達RUB5兆。

加彭提出2027年對外借款約CFA1.1兆、折合$19億的計畫，另擬從國內或區域市場籌措CFA6,000億。預算草案規劃國庫及融資來源共CFA2.9兆，高於2026年的CFA2.3兆；國家收入為CFA3.3兆，債務攤還則為CFA1.9兆。稽核將2025年底估計債務從近CFA11.7兆下修至CFA9.5兆，約占GDP的69%，但融資計畫仍需取得可觀的市場資金。加彭7月已透過一筆$9.2億、7年期、定價9.375%的債券重返國際市場，目前正尋求新的國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）計畫。

委內瑞拉則為債務協商採取外交行動。臨時總統Delcy Rodriguez在美國會談期間，分別會見美洲開發銀行（IDB）總裁Ilan Goldfajn、IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva及世界銀行總裁Ajay Banga。路透消息人士表示，重整、資金與付款是主要焦點。委內瑞拉5月已宣布，計畫重整主權及委內瑞拉國家石油公司（PDVSA）債務，分析師估計金額介於$1,500億至$2,000億。IDB正在準備為期兩年的合作計畫，涵蓋總體經濟資料、電力及社會保障。

IMF與世界銀行同時批准修訂共同的低所得國家債務可持續性框架，這是2017年以來首次聯合檢討。新制擴大國內債務與長期發展挑戰的分析，強化預測及壓力測試，但維持5%折現率，預計2027年下半年上路。路透引述IMF資料指出，約14%的低所得國家已陷入債務困境，另有33%處於高風險。塞內加爾目前仍按現行框架評估；IMF尚未說明，新制對國內債務的處理可能如何影響該國重整。

## 後續市場觀察

9月22日$690億2年期美國公債標售，將面對週一未隨長端上漲的短端市場；9月23日接續標售$700億5年期公債，9月24日則有7年期供給。在Goolsbee與Musalem發出警告後，需求重點是買方是否接受目前短端殖利率，或即使油價下跌，仍要求更高殖利率。John Williams週二及Beth Hammack本週稍晚的發言，將進一步釐清聯準會內部有多少官員同樣重視持續緊縮。

新經濟活動數據將與公債供給同步到來。9月22日有ADP每週就業估計，前值為16,250；同日里奇蒙製造業調查預期為5，前值4。9月23日標普全球PMI初值，製造業預期53.5、前值53.9，服務業預期56、前值56.5。芝加哥活動指數轉弱之後，這些調查所呈現的景氣廣度尤其重要，特別是招聘與需求若放緩，投入成本卻仍居高不下。9月24日初領失業救濟金人數預期20.3萬，前值19.6萬；週五接續公布9月密西根大學消費者信心終值，市場預期47.5，前值51.7。

習近平9月23日至25日訪美，將使貿易休戰、關稅與關鍵礦物取得，和新同意的AI對話一同進入議程。外交氣氛雖已改善，經濟效果仍取決於協議條件能否降低實際貿易與投資的不確定性。若川普與Pezeshkian在聯合國大會當週會面，處理的則是另一項風險：海灣出口增加能否持續緩解能源壓力，而非只是能源衝擊中的又一次短暫喘息。

南非9月23日決策將有助判斷，若央行升息，究竟是預防性行動，還是如美國銀行所預測，代表較長一輪緊縮的開端。非洲其他即將公布的決策，大多預期維持高利率：週二奈及利亞預估維持26.5%，摩洛哥維持2.25%，埃及則可能將19%維持至年底。即使先前通膨降溫曾提供寬鬆空間，能源成本與天候相關的糧食風險仍限制降息。

初級信用市場也有眼前的考驗。Digital Drive預計週三定價，軟銀預計週四進行交易，將分別確立兩種AI曝險的成本：以未來租戶合約支持的建設融資，以及用於股權投資的無擔保借款。AMC再融資則將顯示，票房收入改善能在多大程度上換得可持續的融資條件。結果既取決於投資人對個別發行人的需求，也取決於週一美國公債漲勢能否在本週數據與供給的考驗下延續。

overall_summary.headline: 油價下跌帶動較長天期美債上漲，聯準會警告使短端殖利率難降
overall_summary.session_narrative:
9月21日紐約收盤，10年期美國公債殖利率下降5個基點至4.96%，2年期則維持4.76%。川普釋出願與伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian會面的訊號，加上沙烏地阿拉伯海灣港口裝船量增加，帶動油價大跌，但荷莫茲海峽航運仍嚴重受阻。10年期實質殖利率下降6個基點，通膨補償卻略升，尚不足以顯示通膨壓力獲得持久緩解。

Goolsbee警告，反覆出現的供給衝擊可能需要以令經濟承受痛苦的緊縮政策應對，Musalem則認為聯準會政策仍屬寬鬆。即使芝加哥聯準銀行活動數據偏弱，兩人對持續性通膨的重視，仍有助解釋短端何以未加入漲勢。Meta的AI代理程式帶動科技股領軍股市復甦，美國高收益債利差則變動不大。

借款人持續進入市場籌資：軟銀啟動逾$110億債券發行，部分用於對OpenAI的投資；AMC則在票房收入改善後，再次嘗試再融資。卡達雖然液化天然氣收入驟減，仍憑藉雄厚財務緩衝，以較初步指引收窄約30個基點的利差募得$30億。本週美國公債標售與經濟活動數據，將檢驗在政策仍有進一步緊縮壓力之際，較長端殖利率能否維持低檔。
overall_summary.summary: 外交斡旋的希望緩和了能源衝擊，但美國公債回升來自實質殖利率下降，而非通膨補償回落；主要借款人仍在融資成本提高之際持續籌資。

section_summaries.summary: 美國公債漲勢隨天期拉長而增強，推動力是實質殖利率下降，而非通膨補償降低。沙烏地阿拉伯裝船量增加及美伊外交斡旋的希望促使油價回落，但荷莫茲海峽通行量仍遠低於戰前。芝加哥活動數據轉弱，並未改變Goolsbee與Musalem對持續性通膨可能需要更多緊縮的警告。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Longer-dated Treasuries rallied on September 21 as falling oil prices and renewed diplomatic hopes eased pressure on global markets, but short-term yields held firm as Federal Reserve officials argued that inflation still required restraint. The 10-year yield fell 5 basis points to 4.96%, back below 5%, while the 2-year was unchanged at 4.76%. The recovery extended to equities as enthusiasm for Meta's artificial-intelligence agent lifted technology shares. U.S. high-yield credit spreads were little changed.

The bond rally was concentrated in lower real yields, not a retreat in long-term inflation compensation. That distinction fit a session in which cheaper energy brought relief without settling the policy debate: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warned that repeated supply shocks could require economically painful tightening, and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said policy remained accommodative. Borrowers nevertheless pressed ahead. SoftBank launched a more than $11 billion financing for its OpenAI investment, while Qatar secured $3 billion at spreads substantially below initial indications despite the war's damage to its export revenue.

## Treasury Relief Stops Short of the Front End

The Treasury recovery strengthened with maturity. The 5-year yield declined 3 basis points to 4.83%, and the 30-year fell 5 basis points to 5.29%. With the 2-year stationary, the 2s10s curve narrowed 5 basis points to 20. Over the month, the 2-year yield remained 52 basis points higher, compared with a 22-basis-point increase at 10 years. Monday's buying reduced longer-term borrowing costs while leaving the accumulated repricing of near-term Fed policy largely intact.

The 10-year TIPS real yield fell 6 basis points to 2.62%, while the corresponding breakeven rose 1 basis point to 2.34%. Lower nominal yields therefore came from the real-rate component even as oil retreated sharply. At the 5 p.m. New York fixed-income close, Brent futures stood at $96.12 a barrel, down 7.46%, and WTI at $92.06, down 8.22%. The energy decline eased an immediate burden on consumers and companies without producing a parallel decline in the market's long-run inflation compensation.

President Donald Trump's statement that he would probably be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the United Nations General Assembly encouraged hopes of diplomacy. Satellite observations also showed Saudi oil loadings inside the Persian Gulf increasing over the weekend, with the largest number of ships at the country's main Gulf port since June. Those developments gave the decline in crude a concrete supply and diplomatic backdrop.

Shipping remained severely disrupted. Reuters counted 17 commodity vessels passing through Hormuz over the weekend, against 37 a week earlier; before the war began on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large commercial vessels a day. Visible movements do not capture all exports because some tankers travel with their transponders off. In the week of September 13, 22 tankers, mostly very large crude carriers, carried 42 million barrels out of the strait, with Saudi Arabia and Iraq each accounting for 43% of that volume. There had been no visible oil loadings at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea port of Yanbu since September 16.

U.S.-China negotiations supplied a separate improvement in sentiment. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said weekend discussions with Vice Premier He Lifeng and other officials had agreed on an AI dialogue to establish common understandings of goals and threats. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said a Board of Trade had been put into operation, potentially covering a limited group of non-sensitive goods: Chinese consumer and low-technology products, and U.S. energy, agricultural and medical products. The Financial Times reported that the talks had not extended the trade truce, leaving a substantive decision for the leaders' meeting.

The day's U.S. activity release was softer. The Chicago Fed National Activity Index fell to -0.04 in August from a revised 0.08, below a forecast of 0.2. That added a weaker broad growth observation to the policy debate, but the two Fed speakers focused on why persistent inflation could still warrant further action.

Goolsbee, speaking in London on Monday, argued that supply disturbances were arriving more frequently, lasting longer and doing greater damage. Repeated shocks could no longer simply be treated as temporary changes in the price level. He said restoring price stability might require the Fed to reduce demand even outside the sectors where costs were initially rising, with losses in employment, wages and growth among the possible consequences.

His qualification was important: the appropriate response need not be as forceful as tightening against overheating demand. Nevertheless, accepting repeated, persistent shocks without responding would fail the price-stability mandate. That argument opposed the administration's contention that the Fed should avoid increasing rates into an energy shock. It also exposed a difference with Chairman Kevin Warsh, who had said after the policy meeting that reaching 2% inflation need not require damage to the labor market.

Musalem made a more direct case for additional restraint in a Reuters interview. The St. Louis president, who does not vote on the FOMC this year, judged the current 3.75%-4.00% target range to remain accommodative. Without further tightening, he thought inflation was more likely to remain substantially above 2% in 18 months than to reach the target. Underlying inflation excluding oil and other supply-related effects was perhaps 1 percentage point above target and moving in the wrong direction, he said. July PCE inflation was 3.7% year over year, compared with the recent low of 2.3% in April 2025.

He favored earlier, incremental increases as less disruptive than larger action after inflation became more entrenched, without specifying the next move or a terminal rate. Together, the speeches explained why a better energy session did not remove the pressure on short maturities: both officials regarded the persistence of the inflation process as a separate problem from the latest oil price.

Equities benefited more broadly. The S&P 500 rose 1.49% to 7,764.70, the Nasdaq 100 gained 2.83%, and the semiconductor index advanced 4.29%. Meta gained 11% as its Muse agent's popularity revived expectations for computing demand; AMD rose 10% and closed above $1 trillion in market capitalization for the first time. The Dollar Index rose 0.20% to 100.425, while gold futures fell 0.51% to $4,402.20 an ounce. The combination was a recovery in bonds and technology-led risk appetite rather than a generalized retreat from the dollar.

## AI Borrowing Expands as Investors Question the Terms

SoftBank moved from prospective financing discussions to a defined bond launch, seeking $10 billion of dollar senior unsecured notes and EUR1 billion of euro notes. The dollar securities span 3.5-, 5.5- and 7.5-year maturities, while the euro debt comprises 4- and 6-year tranches. At roughly $11.15 billion equivalent, the planned transaction would exceed 7-Eleven's $10.93 billion January 2021 sale as the largest Asia-Pacific and Japanese non-financial corporate bond offering on record.

The proceeds are intended to fund the $10 billion third tranche of SoftBank's follow-on OpenAI investment, expected to close October 1, and general corporate purposes. The bonds will replace a previously secured $10 billion bridge facility. Pricing is expected September 24, with settlement September 29, and Fitch assigned the proposed notes a BB+ rating. The move places a substantial unsecured financing before public-market investors after SoftBank's earlier expansion of collateral-backed borrowing capacity.

The size also adds to an already heavy year of issuance: SoftBank had sold almost $15 billion of notes across currencies before this transaction, making it the largest junk-rated bond borrower of 2026, according to Bloomberg. Its 2031 dollar bond yielded 8.2% earlier this month, against a January low of 6.7%, as both its spread and underlying Treasury yields rose. The new offering therefore tests demand for more exposure at a time when financing an AI investment has become more expensive even as equity enthusiasm revives.

Later Monday, a separate roughly $1.1 billion junk-bond financing was being marketed for Digital Drive, a data-center project near Richmond, Virginia. Banks led by Goldman Sachs were seeking funding for construction sponsored by affiliates of Blue Owl Capital, Cedarwood Investment Group and PowerHouse Data Centers. Early yield discussions were in the low- to mid-9% area. The offering was reported after the U.S. fixed-income close.

The project's entire 76 megawatts of IT capacity will be leased to CoreWeave under a 15-year, $2.94 billion contract, with operations expected to begin between 2027 and 2028. That contract provides a long revenue commitment, but funding is needed before the facility operates, and investors have been requiring higher yields for projects whose tenants lack investment-grade ratings. An investor call is scheduled for Tuesday at 10 a.m. New York time, with pricing expected Wednesday.

Fidelity International's James Durance offered a skeptical assessment of the sector's debt expansion. The manager, who oversees $14 billion, has kept technology exposure below 2% across his income strategies. He sees the amount of lending itself becoming a source of risk by the end of next year. His global income and short-duration strategies are not tied to benchmarks, allowing him to avoid the growing sector without having to respond to an expanding index weight.

Durance's concern extends beyond individual defaults. Companies have made enormous spending commitments for this year and next without guiding much further ahead. If the resulting investment fails to produce adequate returns, growth expectations and risk assets could suffer together. He does not regard an AI-driven recession as his base case, but notes that hyperscaler debt carries disproportionately long duration relative to its size. A Bloomberg technology-debt gauge has lost about 2.4% over the past year, compared with a 1.3% decline in the broader global aggregate index.

He has instead allocated to UK bank and corporate debt across investment grade and high yield, as well as selected hard-currency emerging-market borrowers. Those holdings include Turkey's Akbank and Turkcell and sovereign debt from Mexico, Romania and the Philippines. His allocation illustrates an investor response to the scale and valuation of AI financing, even as new transactions continue to find their way to market.

ECB Governing Council member Fabio Panetta added a different concern in a Monday speech. Optimistic expectations for AI profitability help technology companies raise capital and keep investing, he said, but leave valuations vulnerable if earnings disappoint. Bank of Italy calculations suggest widespread adoption could raise Italian labor-productivity growth by more than 1 percentage point a year. Panetta emphasized that the demand and inflation consequences depend on who receives those gains.

If new tasks and higher expected labor income make households more confident, consumption could reinforce the investment boom and prolong inflation. If automation instead increases job and wage insecurity, higher saving and weaker spending could bring disinflation sooner. His distinction puts the distribution of productivity gains alongside their size, rather than assuming every increase in AI investment has the same monetary-policy consequences.

Fresh research also quantified a constraint on physical delivery. Data Center Watch reported that local opposition blocked or delayed 45 U.S. projects worth $68 billion between April and June. Communities were adopting construction moratoriums, sometimes before developers applied for permits, while about 30 statehouses introduced or adopted rules covering siting, electricity or water. The findings concern that earlier quarter, but add a concrete measure of execution risk to financing plans dependent on future operating dates.

Power infrastructure is drawing investment well beyond the data centers themselves. BloombergNEF put renewable-energy investment outside China at $247 billion in the first half of 2026, up 15% from a year earlier. Solar and battery storage represented 70% of electricity-generating capacity added in that period. European regulators estimate that the region's aging grid requires EUR600 billion of investment through 2030. The expansion widens the capital requirement associated with computing demand while also responding to energy insecurity; Bloomberg reported that the Iran war had accelerated renewables and storage projects in more than 10 countries, including the Philippines and Thailand.

## Refinancing Reopens Beyond Technology

AMC Entertainment launched a capital-structure overhaul approaching $4 billion after a strong summer at the box office. The cinema operator began a $2 billion junk-bond offering and an $850 million leveraged-loan sale, and signed a commitment letter with Deutsche Bank for a $1.12 billion second-lien loan. Initial discussion for the bonds was in the low-9% yield area.

The operating improvement is substantial. AMC said consolidated revenue rose 42% in July and August from a year earlier to $1.33 billion, with attendance up 36%. U.S. and Canadian cinemas sold a record $4.77 billion of tickets over the summer, according to Rentrak. The company is seeking to use that recovery to replace term loans due in 2029 and 2031 and notes from AMC and its Muvico subsidiary due in 2029.

Six months earlier, adverse conditions had forced AMC to abandon a bond-and-loan refinancing. It relied instead on a $425 million transaction with Deutsche Bank's Distressed Products Group containing provisions for repayment on more favorable terms if a broader refinancing became possible. Corporate borrowings stood at $3.7 billion on June 30. Monday's launch thus represents a renewed attempt to refinance against improved operating results, with the final cost still to be determined.

Nuveen began investor calls for its first sterling bond sale and three dollar issues to help finance the acquisition of Schroders. The sterling tranche is planned as a five-year bond. Nuveen, TIAA's investment manager, agreed earlier this year to pay GBP9.9 billion for Schroders, creating an active manager with nearly $2.5 trillion in combined assets. It had signed a facility of up to GBP3.1 billion with BNP Paribas for the acquisition; the new bonds would fund part of the cash requirement and general corporate purposes. BNP Paribas is global coordinator, with BofA Securities and JPMorgan as joint bookrunners.

In European telecoms, Goldman Sachs traders identified shorter-maturity debt as a way to benefit from company-specific improvements at Virgin Media O2 and VodafoneZiggo. Their assessment focused on Virgin Media O2's 2029 bonds and VodafoneZiggo's 2030 notes after management meetings at a leveraged-finance conference. The companies have more than $15 billion and almost $8 billion of bonds outstanding, respectively, and face intensifying competition from alternative fiber networks.

For Virgin Media O2, the traders cited potential AI-related cost savings and its planned acquisition of Netomnia. At VodafoneZiggo, they pointed to cash generation through disposals, including an agreed EUR669 million sale of mobile towers, and improving subscriber trends after pricing and contract changes. Management is targeting a listing of the wider group by mid-2027 following its combination with Telenet. Those proposed sources of support address debt that sold off sharply in July as investors questioned earnings and debt-service capacity.

Mexico's Fibra Educa is seeking authorization for MXN3 billion-MXN3.5 billion of additional local issuance by year-end, through reopening bonds sold in June. Chief Executive Raul Martinez Solares said proceeds would finance campus acquisitions and possible development, either directly or by repaying a MXN2.5 billion revolver used for purchases. Investors meet Tuesday to consider access to the full MXN20 billion debt program established in 2023; the trust has reached the MXN12 billion cap applying during its first five years. Regulatory approvals are also required. Management is examining international borrowing, but peso revenues make the exchange-rate exposure or hedging cost a substantive constraint.

Securitized markets were offering favorable issuance conditions. Truist's Brock Wolf forecast that U.S. asset-backed securities sales could rise as much as 15% this year and a further 10% in 2027. Volume has already exceeded $300 billion for a third consecutive year and is 11% ahead of the corresponding 2025 pace. Spreads are the narrowest in more than four years. Wolf expects data-center spending and banks' synthetic risk transfers to be important sources of supply, while identifying oil and the Fed's inflation response as the principal uncertainties.

A separate legal filing exposed concentrated receivables-financing risk at troubled commodity trader Radiant World. The company disclosed $870 million owed to six creditors, with Jefferies and Intesa Sanpaolo carrying the largest exposures, followed by Deutsche Bank, Mizuho, Mariner Investment Group and Incomlend. The disclosure identifies the lenders and amount at risk without establishing recoveries.

European settlement infrastructure also changed Monday. The ECB opened Pontes, linking blockchain markets to existing euro-area payment systems so banks can settle tokenized wholesale transactions in central-bank money. An initial group of participants and distributed-ledger operators was ready to use the system immediately, with others planning connections in the coming months. A longer-term successor, Appia, is due to have a blueprint in 2028. The launch brings central-bank settlement to these transactions separately from the planned retail digital euro.

## Rate-Hike Risks Split Across Canada, Korea and South Africa

Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem sharpened his warning about waiting too long to respond to persistent inflation. In Halifax on Monday, he said delaying necessary tightening could force both a faster pace of increases and a higher eventual rate. But he also emphasized the cost of acting unnecessarily: raising rates when price pressure remains contained would weaken growth without a corresponding benefit.

The bank is assessing whether its 2.25% policy rate will return inflation to 2%. Macklem said annual consumer-price growth had remained around 3%, largely because of gasoline, and could edge higher in the coming months if oil stayed near $100 a barrel. His warning made the duration of the shock central to the decision, not merely its initial effect on headline prices.

He supplied a new estimate of the growth damage from U.S. trade restrictions: if the latest tariffs remain, Q4 growth could be roughly halved to below 1%. The direct aggregate exposure is limited to products representing about 5% of Canada's goods exports to the United States, with federal support mitigating some harm. The broader risk is that uncertainty postpones hiring and investment. A new forecasting model, Prima, will first be used in October's Monetary Policy Report to help examine alternative scenarios and separate temporary from persistent price pressure.

In South Korea, JPMorgan economist Seok Gil Park saw upside risk even to the bank's above-consensus forecast of a 3.75% terminal rate, provided credit and financial markets remain stable. Its expected path includes increases in November, February and May, from the current 3%. That compares with a Bloomberg economist-survey median of 3.5%, held through Q2 2028.

The bank's growth outlook explains the difference. Park forecasts expansion of 3.8% this year and 3.3% next year, against the Bank of Korea's 3.3% and 2.9%. For Q3, JPMorgan expects about 1% quarter-on-quarter growth, compared with the BOK's roughly 0.3%. The chip boom is already visible in investment; whether it spreads through suppliers, wages and household spending will determine how much additional domestic inflation follows.

Park is watching elevated monthly gains in non-petroleum manufactured goods and personal services. A stronger won reduces import costs, but he argued that appreciation arising from better terms of trade and higher real incomes can also support demand. Large chipmaker bonuses alone may have a limited consumption effect because the direct beneficiaries are a relatively small share of workers. The policy question turns on the breadth of the income gains rather than semiconductor exports alone.

South African forecasts moved toward more tightening despite a recent improvement in surveyed inflation expectations. Morgan Stanley's Andrea Masia and Arnav Gupta changed their September 23 call from a hold to a 25-basis-point increase to 7.25%. They described it as insurance against renewed oil pressure prolonging the period above the 3% target, rather than a response to an observed deterioration in expectations or broad pass-through across consumer prices.

Higher inflation also reduces the real restraint delivered by an unchanged nominal rate. Morgan Stanley expects the SARB to hold after that increase through 2027, seeing limited room for short rates to incorporate the roughly 75 basis points of additional tightening priced by markets.

Bank of America's Tatonga Rusike now expects two increases, in September and November, taking the repo rate to 7.5%, rather than the single move previously anticipated. He raised the inflation outlook to an average 5% in Q4 and a 5.3% peak in Q1 2027, and expects easing to be delayed until the second half of 2027. The contrast is with survey expectations that had edged down to 3.8% from 3.9%: the more hawkish forecasts respond to prospective oil effects rather than a newly reported unanchoring of expectations.

Brazil's weekly central-bank survey moved in the opposite direction. Analysts lowered their end-2026 Selic forecast to 13.5% from 13.75%, following last week's cut to 13.75%, while leaving the 2027 and 2028 forecasts at 12% and 10.50%. Further easing depends partly on the fiscal and currency consequences of the close presidential election between Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro. Plans for public debt and spending could affect the real and inflation even as domestic activity cools.

China's currency strengthened independently of the firmer U.S. dollar. The onshore yuan reached 6.6950 per dollar and closed at 6.6955, its strongest domestic close since June 2022. The PBOC set its midpoint at 6.7487, still 536 pips weaker than Reuters' estimate, but has strengthened it faster during September and narrowed the gap with market expectations. The adjustment signals less resistance to gradual appreciation within the currency's 2% trading band.

## Sovereign Borrowers Face Sharply Different Financing Conditions

Qatar completed its first public international bond sale since November, raising $3 billion across five- and 10-year maturities. The tranches priced at 55 and 65 basis points over Treasuries, respectively, each about 30 basis points tighter than initial price thoughts. Orders peaked above $7.7 billion before easing to about $6.8 billion. Peak demand exceeded $3 billion for the five-year, excluding joint lead managers' interest, and $4.7 billion for the 10-year.

The reception contrasted with a severe loss of export income. LNG revenue fell to $200 million in Q2 from $9 billion in Q1 as disruption at Hormuz impaired Qatar's main export route. The government recorded a $5.8 billion quarterly deficit, equivalent to 11.4% of quarterly GDP, while revenue fell 57% from a year earlier, according to JPMorgan. Economists in Bloomberg's survey expect the economy to contract 12.1% this year.

Qatar nevertheless retains substantial financial buffers, including a $580 billion sovereign wealth fund and more than $70 billion of foreign-exchange reserves, alongside an AA rating from S&P. Its investment agenda is also continuing. The government announced Doha Investment to manage and expand the wealth fund's domestic portfolio and plans about $38.5 billion of infrastructure awards over five years, including public-private partnerships. The Qatar Investment Authority is targeting a $20 billion partnership with JPMorgan, including $15 billion for public equities and $5 billion for private investment in U.S. middle-market companies. Those plans coexist with the immediate fiscal shock rather than removing it.

Chile supplied new evidence of foreign demand for local sovereign debt. Nonresident peso-bond holdings rose $700 million in August to a record $21.04 billion, a 42% increase since the start of the year. That substantially exceeded the gains reported for Colombia, at 4.2% through August, and Brazil and Mexico, at about 2% and 3% through July.

Fiscal performance helps explain the attraction. Chile posted a CLP95 billion surplus in July against a CLP957 billion deficit a year earlier, with private-mining revenue up 79% and spending down 0.7%. Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz plans to limit spending growth to 0%-1% next year. Banco Itau's Andres Perez said elevated metals prices and restrained expenditure were strengthening the credibility of consolidation after years of above-target deficits.

Market-access reforms could support that demand. The government is seeking to let pension funds conduct repo and reverse-repo transactions for the first time and has put a market-maker program out for consultation. The pension proposal forms part of 30 capital-market measures that also address paperwork and tax hurdles for foreign investors. Banco de Credito e Inversiones' Alexis Vega expects repo financing to reduce investment costs and market-making to improve Treasury-debt liquidity.

Poland's first trading response to Friday's Moody's downgrade was comparatively calm. The 2036 dollar-bond yield fell 4 basis points to 5.86% Monday, and the local 10-year premium over Germany narrowed to 273 basis points in morning Warsaw trading from the preceding week's 289-basis-point peak. The zloty was 0.1% stronger against the euro. The move to A3 had not triggered an immediate additional selloff, even as political disagreement continued to obstruct fiscal consolidation.

The European Fiscal Board issued a broader warning about enforcement. Repeated flexibility and escape clauses risk weakening the rules introduced in April 2024, it said. Those rules give countries four to seven years to move toward the EU's 3% deficit and 60% debt limits. The board said no comply-or-explain statements had been issued and only Bulgaria had faced procedural consequences through a new excessive-deficit procedure. EU debt rose to 82% of GDP in 2025 from 81% in 2024, and the Commission forecasts more than 84% this year.

Russia also increased its financing requirement. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said the 2026 deficit would reach 3% of GDP, compared with the 1.6% plan and 2.6% in 2025. The January-August shortfall had already reached 2.5%. Borrowing will exceed the original RUB5.5 trillion plan, supplemented by unused funds from previous years. Higher oil prices and a weaker ruble have increased export-related revenue without preventing the deterioration, while high rates raise debt-service costs. Siluanov still expects National Wealth Fund reserves to rise by RUB600 billion-RUB1 trillion to RUB5 trillion by year-end.

Gabon proposed about CFA1.1 trillion, or $1.9 billion, of external borrowing for 2027, plus CFA600 billion from domestic or regional markets. The draft budget envisages CFA2.9 trillion of treasury and financing resources, up from CFA2.3 trillion in 2026, against CFA3.3 trillion of state revenue and CFA1.9 trillion of debt amortization. An audit reduced estimated end-2025 debt to CFA9.5 trillion from almost CFA11.7 trillion, or about 69% of GDP, but the financing plan still requires substantial market access. Gabon is seeking a new IMF program after returning to international markets in July with a $920 million seven-year bond priced at 9.375%.

Venezuela took a diplomatic step toward its own debt negotiations. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez met IDB President Ilan Goldfajn, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and World Bank President Ajay Banga separately during U.S. discussions. A Reuters source said restructuring, funds and payments were a major focus. The engagement follows Venezuela's May announcement of plans to restructure sovereign and PDVSA obligations estimated by analysts at $150 billion-$200 billion. The IDB is preparing a two-year engagement plan, including work on macroeconomic data, electricity and social protection.

The IMF and World Bank meanwhile approved changes to their joint low-income-country debt-sustainability framework, the first joint review since 2017. The revisions expand analysis of domestic debt and long-term development challenges and strengthen forecasting and stress tests, while retaining the 5% discount rate. They are scheduled to become operational in H2 2027. About 14% of low-income countries are in distress and another 33% at high risk, according to IMF data cited by Reuters. Senegal will still be assessed under the existing framework for now; the IMF has not set out how the new domestic-debt treatment could affect its restructuring.

## Forward Market Significance

The September 22 auction of $69 billion of 2-year Treasuries now meets a front end that failed to join Monday's rally. A $70 billion five-year sale follows September 23, with seven-year supply on September 24. The relevant demand question is whether buyers accept the short-rate compensation after Goolsbee and Musalem's warnings, or require higher yields even as oil falls. John Williams' Tuesday remarks and Beth Hammack's comments later in the week can further define how widely their emphasis on persistent restraint is shared.

Fresh activity evidence will arrive alongside that supply. September 22 brings ADP's weekly employment estimate, following 16,250 previously, and the Richmond manufacturing survey, where consensus is 5 against a prior 4. September 23 flash S&P PMIs are expected at 53.5 for manufacturing after 53.9 and 56 for services after 56.5. Their breadth matters after the weaker Chicago activity reading, especially if hiring and demand soften while input costs remain elevated. September 24 initial claims are expected at 203,000 after 196,000; the final September Michigan sentiment reading follows Friday, with consensus at 47.5 against the prior 51.7.

Xi Jinping's September 23-25 U.S. visit puts the trade truce, tariffs and critical-mineral access alongside the newly agreed AI dialogue. The opening diplomatic tone has improved, but the economic consequences depend on terms that reduce uncertainty for actual trade and investment. Any Trump-Pezeshkian meeting during UN week would address a different risk: whether increased Gulf exports can become sustained relief rather than another temporary interruption in the energy shock.

South Africa's September 23 decision will distinguish an insurance increase from the start of the larger tightening sequence now forecast by Bank of America. Elsewhere in Africa, the coming decisions are predominantly expected to preserve high rates: Nigeria is expected to hold at 26.5% and Morocco at 2.25% on Tuesday, while Egypt could retain 19% through year-end. Energy costs and weather-related food risks constrain easing even where earlier disinflation had created room.

Primary credit supplies its own immediate tests. Digital Drive's expected Wednesday pricing and SoftBank's expected Thursday transaction will establish the cost of two different AI exposures, construction backed by a future tenant contract and unsecured borrowing funding an equity investment. AMC's refinancing will show how far improved ticket revenue translates into sustainable financing terms. Their outcome will depend on issuer-specific demand as well as whether Monday's Treasury recovery survives the week's data and supply.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
The 10-year Treasury yield fell 5 basis points to 4.96% at the September 21 New York close, while the 2-year held at 4.76%. Oil fell sharply as Trump signaled openness to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Saudi Gulf loadings increased. Shipping through Hormuz nevertheless remained severely disrupted. The 10-year real yield declined 6 basis points, while inflation compensation edged higher, limiting the evidence of lasting inflation relief.

Goolsbee warned that repeated supply shocks could require economically painful tightening, and Musalem judged Fed policy still accommodative. Their emphasis on persistent inflation helped explain why short maturities did not join the rally, even after a softer Chicago Fed activity reading. Meta's AI agent drove a technology-led equity recovery, while U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed.

Borrowers continued to access markets: SoftBank launched more than $11 billion of bonds to help fund its OpenAI investment, and AMC reopened a refinancing attempt after stronger box-office revenue. Qatar raised $3 billion at spreads about 30 basis points below initial indications despite a collapse in LNG revenue, supported by substantial financial buffers. The week's Treasury auctions and activity data will test whether lower longer-term yields can persist alongside pressure for further policy restraint.
